claims.text: the hit set holds every reference to afk:fix, afk:bug over the name forms this pass searched

/afk:fix ends with two lines, not one: `OUTCOME: <status> — <one-line summary> [ticket: <KEY|none>]` then `In plain terms: …`, and the OUTCOME: line gains `[miss: <class>]` and `[lesson: <L-NNNN>]` when Phases 2.5 and 3.5 ran; only when an orchestrator parses the trailing line does the plain-terms line go first, so the OUTCOME: line ends the report.

/afk:fix never commits, pushes or merges: it applies its edits and leaves the commit to the human or the calling run; its OUTCOME: status is fixed, fixed_no_test, cannot_reproduce, design_conflict, needs_artifact_sync or blocked, blocked covering anything else.

Five plugin-source sites run /afk:fix: /afk:execute Step 8 for a verification tier still red after one retry, Step 10 for correctness and spec review findings, Step 10.5 for critical or high adversary findings, and /afk:preflight PF-3 and PF-4 for correctness and spec findings; the /afk:bug fixer prompt is the sixth caller. /afk:fix names a red smoke gate as a trigger, but no /afk:smoke-test line names /afk:fix.

Steps 10 and 10.5 and PF-3 and PF-4 read no /afk:fix status and end on their own caps: review_fail, adversary_fail after 2 cycles, park(PF-3: review_stalemate), and park(PF-4: orphan_artifact) once the shared counter of 2 is spent.

claims.text: One caller of /afk:fix already stops for the developer and resumes the same run: the /afk:bug fixer runs /afk:fix, and its BUGFIX: blocked moves the bug S4→S5, sends a push notification and resumes the same fixer with its context on the answer; today that path carries a structured question, not a design, and the fixer prompt names only non-reproduction as a blocked cause and maps no /afk:fix status to a BUGFIX: token.

No caller of /afk:fix under /afk:execute or /afk:preflight carries a design to the human and resumes the same fix after the answer: a design stop ending as blocked becomes test_fail at Step 8, an open finding that runs to review_fail at Step 10 or a park at PF-3, a spent cycle ending in adversary_fail at Step 10.5, and a park at PF-4; a park notification names the status and one plain sentence, not the design.

In a hands-off run no human can answer a design stop: execute's driven mode never pauses for input and turns a one-way door into a failure status, and the autopilot child may not wait for input. AC-032 says a stage with no human present runs as it does today, AC-037 says afk-lite runs for /afk:fix, and neither row names the other, so which one governs a driven /afk:execute or an auto-chained /afk:preflight is open.

execute's hard rule reads every verdict from the spawning call's own result and forbids waiting on a child's completion notification; an /afk:fix team that returns through a result file and a finished message the requester waits for on its inbox (S-154) contradicts that rule at Steps 8, 10 and 10.5, and row 4 does not name it.

The callers' commit steps today: Step 10 commits each round's remediation as `[{NNNN-slug}] review fix: …` and pushes; Step 10.5 commits and pushes before it re-runs from Step 8; PF-3 commits through the settle loop's round close, which follows the caller's commit rules, and preflight runs its ancestry guard before every push; the /afk:bug fixer commits, pushes and opens a Draft change once the fix and its test are green. Step 8 and PF-4 name no commit after /afk:fix, and execute's commit contract names Steps 6, 10 and 11.

Row 4's rule that the callers keep their commit steps matches today's contract, because /afk:fix already ends with uncommitted edits; the edits /afk:fix leaves at Step 8 and PF-4 wait for a later commit today, a gap that exists before the change.

What reaches /afk:fix today is its caller's conversation: its argument may be nothing, with the finding inferred from the conversation, and an ad-hoc finding is taken from the conversation with no delegation. A pane agent gets its duties only in its launch prompt and later data by message (S-150), so each caller must write the finding into the brief, and the 'nothing' form stops working.

Two outputs of today's run have no carrier to the caller under a pane team: Phase 3's 'surface to the /afk:execute run' for a shifted subtask contract, and /afk:diagnose's rule that the confirmed hypothesis goes into the commit or PR message, which a builder that does not commit cannot meet; the OUTCOME: line carries one summary line.

Phase 2.5 can edit tests: for a weak-assertion, wrong-path or disabled/flaky miss it fixes the existing scenario in place and re-runs it red then green. If the hub runs Phase 2.5 after the review step (S-207), those test edits reach the caller unreviewed by the team, and the agent-class table has no column for editing code.

Phase 3's PRD route ends in /afk:to-ticket, a tracker writer, and the non-contact hub may not write the tracker, so a hub that runs Phase 3 as the skill states it can take only the fallback: record the divergence and report needs_artifact_sync.

Phase 3.5 appends its lesson with `bash $AFK_PLUGIN_ROOT/hooks/lesson-append.sh opened … --writer fix` from the main checkout. The script finds the ledger through the git common directory, so an append from any worktree lands in the main checkout's ledger; it mints the id as the highest id plus one with no lock before the append, and it always exits 0.

The native contract gate scans every plugin *.md except PROVIDERS.md, CAPABILITIES.md and providers/CONFORMANCE.md, its patterns are case-sensitive, and its allow list holds no entry for skills/afk/fix or skills/afk/bug.

Row 4's watch-out that the gate keeps pane-launch commands out of skills/afk/fix overstates it: the gate refuses provider vocabulary in any plugin markdown, not launch commands, so a launch line naming a lowercase binary or a transport passes it.

/afk:fix and /afk:diagnose start more than the spawn list counts: an afk-reader for the Jira pull and another for Phase 3 reads, an afk-runner for bulk runs, and one /afk:investigate run whose tracers are more agents. Whether a pane team member holds the tracker server's registration, which /afk:fix's Jira intake needs, is harness runtime that no repository document states.

/afk:fix reads its session type from the working directory's branch and plan directory; every team agent starts in the run's worktree (S-152) while the /afk:bug fixer may write only inside its own worktree. The repository does not say which worktree the team of a fixer starts in; if it is not the fixer's, the session type and the fixer's write rule both fail.

The /afk:bug fixer runs /afk:fix, commits once the fix and its test are green, and returns `BUGFIX: <status> — <summary>` with status mr-ready, fix-pushed, blocked or failed; nothing in its prompt maps an /afk:fix status, and the spawner parses only the BUGFIX: token.

One more plugin-source site names /afk:fix and reads no result line: the lesson ledger format maps the miss class /afk:fix's escape analysis names, carried verbatim in the lesson event's miss field, to a lesson class, in lockstep with skills/afk/fix/ESCAPE-ANALYSIS.md.
/afk:retro and /afk:review name /afk:fix as the remediation route and ROUND.md points at its Phase 2 text; none of them reads a result line, and settle-change's 'fix/dispute' is not the skill.

Provider detection takes four markers, not two: AFK_PROVIDER overrides every other, Codex is detected from PLUGIN_ROOT and Claude from CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT or CLAUDECODE, all pinned by hook-smoke.sh; precommit-gates.sh also exits 0 when AFK_SKIP_PRECOMMIT_GATES=1, before it checks for an agent session.
The commit-time gates run only in an agent session: hooks/precommit-gates.sh exits 0 when no provider is detected.

A pane agent's commit, such as the /afk:bug fixer's, runs the commit-time gates only when AFK_SKIP_PRECOMMIT_GATES is not 1 and its process carries a marker that resolves to a known provider: AFK_PROVIDER naming claude or codex, else PLUGIN_ROOT, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT or CLAUDECODE; an AFK_PROVIDER naming no known provider turns detection off whatever else is set, so a transport that exports AFK_PROVIDER settles it only with a known provider's name.

Which of AFK_PROVIDER, PLUGIN_ROOT, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT or CLAUDECODE the processes a pane transport starts carry is harness runtime outside this repository; hooks/precommit-gates.sh says only that agent runtimes mark the environment of every process they spawn.
Only the agent that runs Phases 2.5 and 3.5 can put the miss class and the lesson id into the OUTCOME: summary, so under S-207 the hub, not the builder, has to write the final OUTCOME: line.
The settle loop's information diet binds the subagent prompts of reviewer, adjudicator and fixer; it does not say whether it binds the launch briefs of a pane team that fixes a finding.

publish_bug.py resolves the tracker kind from the directory it is handed or its working directory, not the git root, and exits at import when that kind lacks the Jira machinery; it reads credentials from JIRA_* variables or from a registration's env block in ~/.claude.json or ~/.codex/config.toml, not from a live MCP session.

The fixer reaches the forge through afk_adapter, which takes the kind from the configuration of the git root its shell runs in; FIXER-PROMPT.md calls afk_adapter without saying to source hooks/lib/adapter.sh, and reaches the Maven lock through $AFK_PLUGIN_ROOT, which the register says the hook launcher exports.
